newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates ends down, spot up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates ends down, spot up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Monday due to reduced demand with few companies due to list on the stock markets in the short term, traders said.

The most active three-day contract rose to 5.00 percent from 2.59 percent. Total turnover surged to 6.64 million lots from last Friday's 3.58 million lots. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said volume increased while rates fell, indicating there was sufficient money supply on the market.
"A lack of new share issues and listings is a key factor for the decline in the rates today," said one trader.
The A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen are the major source of money demand for the repo market.
Traders said the rates were unlikely to rise sharply before a number of new domestic share issues and listings were announced.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up with some long-term investors eager to buy the existing contracts because of the higher yields compared to new debt, traders said.

The coupons for the new debt, the issue of which started on Saturday, are much lower than yields of the existing state debt spot contracts on the Shanghai market, which is the main reason for Monday's gains.
"A large number of long-term investors have bought the existing contracts recently due to their higher yields," said a trader. "The trend is likely to continue in the short term."
The most active three-year bond that matures in August 1999 rose to 105.30 yuan from 104.46 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market surged to 2.62 million lots from last Friday's 1.12 million lots.
